title: Cocido Madrileño
subtitle: Madrid slow-cooked chickpea, meat, and vegetable stew
excerpt: The great slow-cooked stew of Madrid: chickpeas, a whole chicken, chorizo, morcilla, pork belly, and vegetables simmered together in one pot for hours until the broth is deeply flavoured. Served in two or three courses from the same pot.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cocido madrileño is considered the Sunday lunch of Madrid, a descendant of the medieval Sephardic adafina stew that was adapted by Spanish Catholics after 1492. Like the French pot-au-feu and the Italian bollito misto, it is an ancient cooking method of simmering everything in one pot until the pot liquor becomes a clear, gelatinous broth of extraordinary depth. The dish is traditionally served in two or three courses (called vuelcos, or tippings): first the strained broth with fine pasta, then the chickpeas and vegetables, then the meats. The chickpeas must be soaked overnight; tinned chickpeas turn to mush over the long cooking. The morcilla (blood sausage) is a signature element; if unavailable, it can be omitted or replaced with more chorizo.

content.text: Soak the chickpeas overnight in plenty of cold water. Never let the pot boil hard; a hard boil makes the broth cloudy and the chickpeas tough. The correct simmer is barely perceptible, with just the occasional bubble. Skim the surface carefully in the first 20 minutes.

content.text: Put the chickpeas, chicken, pork belly, onion, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a very large pot. Cover with cold water by 8 cm. Bring slowly to a simmer, skimming regularly. Once the foam has cleared (about 20 minutes), add the carrot and chorizo. Reduce to the gentlest simmer. Cook uncovered for 1 hour 30 minutes.

Add the potatoes. Cook for 25 minutes. Add the cabbage and cook for 20 minutes more. Check the chickpeas: they should be completely tender with no chalkiness. Season the broth with salt. Lift out all the meats and vegetables.

Strain the broth and bring to a boil. Cook the pasta in the broth and serve as the first course. Arrange the chickpeas and vegetables on one platter and the sliced meats on another for the second and third courses. Accompany with mustard and pickled peppers.
